articles.title: Five Extra Minutes of Sleep and Two Minutes of Exercise a Day Could Add a Full Year to Your Life
articles.excerpt: A landmark UK Biobank study of nearly 60,000 adults finds that tiny, simultaneous improvements in sleep, physical activity, and diet compound into as much as 9.4 extra years of disease-free living — and the findings carry outsized implications for South Asians.
articles.image_caption: Fresh vegetables, whole grains, and fruits — small dietary improvements that compound over time
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated cardiometabolic risk at lower BMI thresholds — this study shows that even tiny concurrent lifestyle changes can yield outsized health gains for diaspora professionals struggling to make time for wellness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Single Blood Test Can Now Screen for 10 Cancers — and Zydus and Apollo Are Bringing It to India
articles.excerpt: The FDA-designated multi-cancer detection test, built by Guardant Health, uses a simple blood draw to catch bladder, breast, colorectal and seven other cancers before symptoms appear
articles.image_caption: A laboratory technician examines blood sample vials for diagnostic testing
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who schedule health check-ups during visits to India could access a validated multi-cancer blood test through Apollo's nationwide network, and South Asians face distinctive cancer risks that make early multi-cancer screening especially relevant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South Asians Face Elevated Heart Risk by Age 45 Despite Healthier Habits — and the Paradox Runs Deeper Than Diet
articles.excerpt: A landmark US study of 2,700 adults finds that South Asian Americans have nearly eight times the prediabetes rate of white peers by midlife — even with better diets and less alcohol. The risk may start at birth.
articles.image_caption: Cardiovascular screening — new research shows South Asians face elevated heart disease risk by age 45 despite healthier habits (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.label: Journal of the American Heart Association (Feb. 2026)
South Asian Birth Cohort Study, McMaster University

articles.nri_angle: Directly impacts the 5.4 million Indian Americans and broader South Asian diaspora — the study reveals they need earlier cardiovascular screening starting in their 40s, not the standard mid-50s guidelines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Having Weak Muscles and Excess Body Fat Dramatically Raises Your Dementia Risk — and South Asians May Be Uniquely Vulnerable
articles.excerpt: A landmark Curtin University study of nearly 500,000 adults finds sarcopenic obesity is a major dementia driver, while being overweight alone is not — if muscle strength is preserved
articles.image_caption: An older adult performing resistance training, which new research suggests is critical for protecting brain health
articles.nri_angle: South Asians' well-documented 'skinny fat' phenotype — high visceral fat with low muscle mass — places them at elevated risk for the sarcopenic obesity now linked to dementia, making resistance training an urgent priority for NRI health.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Teen's Friends May Shape Their Mental Health More Than You Think — A 600,000-Person Study Shows How
articles.excerpt: A massive Finnish study published in JAMA Psychiatry finds that adolescents whose peers have mental health diagnoses are significantly more likely to develop conditions like anxiety and depression themselves — a finding with urgent implications for diaspora families navigating unfamiliar school systems.
articles.image_caption: Teenagers at school — a 600,000-person Finnish study found peer relationships significantly affect adolescent mental health risk (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI parents raising teenagers in Western school systems face a peer-influence dynamic that differs sharply from Indian schooling — understanding how their child's social environment shapes mental health risk is essential for early intervention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fish Oil Supplements Don't Protect Your Brain From Alzheimer's, a Rigorous Two-Year Trial Finds
articles.excerpt: Americans spend over $1 billion a year on fish oil, but a USC clinical trial shows the supplements fail to slow cognitive decline — even though they reach the brain. For South Asians, the findings raise uncomfortable questions about a supplement many families swear by.
articles.image_caption: Fish oil capsules, among the most popular dietary supplements worldwide
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face rising Alzheimer's risk and are heavy fish oil users — this trial suggests they should shift spending from supplements to whole-food diets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Remote Work Is Making Americans Lonelier and More Depressed — and the Effect Is Worst for Those Who Live Alone
articles.excerpt: A sweeping study of 588,000 workers finds that the shift to working from home accounts for a third of the rise in national mental distress since 2011. For Indian-origin tech workers thousands of miles from family, the findings hit close to home.
articles.image_caption: A remote worker at a home desk — the daily reality for millions in tech and knowledge-economy roles
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech workers in the US are disproportionately in remotable jobs and far from family — making them especially vulnerable to the isolation the study documents.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Older Adults Who Walk Like Someone 30 Years Younger Have Half the Risk of Cognitive Decline — Even With Alzheimer's Pathology
articles.excerpt: A landmark study in Neurology identifies 'super movers' — people over 80 whose brisk gait appears to shield their brains from dementia, offering a deceptively simple biomarker that diaspora families can track as parents age
articles.image_caption: An older adult walking briskly through a park — a habit that new research links to sharply lower dementia risk

sources.label: NBC Palm Springs / Univ. of Minnesota

articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated diabetes and cardiovascular risk that accelerate cognitive decline; walking speed is a culturally familiar, measurable biomarker diaspora families can track as parents age.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three to Four Cups of Coffee a Day Can Halve Your Risk of Liver Cancer — and Decaf Works Too
articles.excerpt: A 354,957-person Cedars-Sinai study finds that moderate coffee drinking — regular or decaf — is linked to dramatically lower rates of cirrhosis, liver cancer and liver-related death, with implications for South Asians facing rising fatty liver disease
articles.image_caption: A freshly brewed cup of coffee — moderate daily consumption has been linked to significantly lower liver cancer and cirrhosis risk
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face rising NAFLD rates — moderate coffee drinking may offer a simple protective intervention aligned with India's filter coffee tradition
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Just 12 Weeks of Time-Restricted Eating Can Keep Weight Off for a Full Year, a New Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A randomised trial from Spain shows that limiting meals to an eight-hour window produces durable weight loss regardless of whether you eat early or late — a flexible strategy that could reshape how South Asians manage obesity.
articles.image_caption: Fresh vegetables and fruits arranged for healthy meal planning — a visual representation of time-restricted eating. (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: South Asians have among the highest rates of metabolic syndrome globally, and a flexible, no-calorie-counting approach to weight management that fits around family mealtimes or shift-work schedules could prove especially practical for diaspora households.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ultra-Processed Foods Are Now Linked to a Doubled Risk of Oesophageal Cancer — and the Threat May Be Greater for Diaspora Indians
articles.excerpt: A new multi-cancer study finds that high UPF intake raises oesophageal cancer risk by 129% and stomach cancer by 56%, adding to evidence that should alarm anyone who has swapped home-cooked dal for packaged meals
articles.image_caption: A bowl of brightly coloured ultra-processed breakfast cereal, a typical NOVA Group 4 food
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora Indians transitioning from traditional home-cooked food to Western ultra-processed diets face compounded gastrointestinal cancer risk on top of already elevated metabolic disease rates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Turmeric's Active Compound Can Ease Depression as Effectively as Some Drugs — and the Evidence Is Growing
articles.excerpt: A meta-analysis presented at the APA 2026 meeting found curcumin supplements produced a 'moderate-to-large' reduction in depressive symptoms across five randomised trials — with zero major side effects reported
articles.image_caption: Turmeric root and curcumin powder, the golden spice now backed by clinical evidence for depression treatment

sources.label: Boston University School of Public Health

articles.nri_angle: Turmeric is the signature spice of Indian kitchens and Ayurveda — this clinical evidence validates ancestral knowledge and gives diaspora families a culturally familiar tool to discuss mental health.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Living in a Walkable Neighbourhood Could Be as Important for Your Health as Diet or Exercise, a Major New Study Finds
articles.excerpt: An MIT-led analysis of 28,000 U.S. census tracts, published in Nature Health, found that urban design — green spaces, mixed-use streets, and short connected blocks — is a powerful and independent predictor of both physical and mental health outcomes
articles.image_caption: Central Park in New York City — walkable green spaces are linked to better physical and mental health outcomes

sources.label: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

articles.nri_angle: For NRIs choosing between US cities and suburbs, this study offers data-backed guidance: walkable, green neighborhoods don't just feel better — they measurably protect your physical and mental health.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Millennials and Gen X Are Aging Faster Biologically Than Their Parents — and a Major Study Links It to Rising Cancer Rates
articles.excerpt: A Nature Medicine analysis of over 150,000 people finds that recent generations show accelerated biological aging, which may help explain the surge in early-onset cancers — a trend with particular implications for South Asians.
articles.image_caption: Biological aging research: Chemical laboratory at the central cancer research labs
articles.nri_angle: South Asians already face elevated metabolic and cancer risks at younger ages; accelerated biological aging in recent generations adds a compounding vulnerability that standard screening timelines may not account for.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nestlé Will Strip Artificial Colourings From Every Product on Earth by Year-End — and It Could Reshape What Indians Eat
articles.excerpt: The Swiss food giant becomes the first major packaged-food company to set a global deadline for eliminating synthetic dyes, a move driven by GLP-1 drug pressure and RFK Jr.'s FDA crackdown that could ripple through Maggi, KitKat, and Munch in India
articles.image_caption: Nestlé products in a retail store — the company plans to remove all artificial colourings from its global portfolio by end-2026
articles.nri_angle: NRIs navigating different food safety standards between the US/UK and India may finally see consistency as Nestlé standardises its ingredient lists globally — including for iconic Indian brands like Maggi and KitKat
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Simultaneous Heat Emergency Is Scorching Two Continents — and Millions of Indian Diaspora Are in Its Path
articles.excerpt: Europe's deadliest heatwave in years has killed over 1,300 people, and now a punishing heat dome is descending on the US for July 4th. For the 7 million-strong Indian diaspora across both regions, the message is the same: this is not normal summer heat.
articles.image_caption: Extreme heat conditions — a simultaneous heatwave is affecting both the United States and South Asia (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Over 6 million Indian-origin residents in the US and UK face record-breaking heat in their home cities, with multigenerational households and elderly family members at acute risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A New Weight-Loss Drug Just Matched Bariatric Surgery — and It Could Change How South Asians Fight Obesity
articles.excerpt: Eli Lilly's retatrutide produced 28% weight loss at 80 weeks in the landmark TRIUMPH-1 trial, the first medication ever to rival surgical outcomes — a potential game-changer for a community with the world's highest metabolic disease burden.
articles.image_caption: An Ozempic injection pen — retatrutide belongs to the same GLP-1 drug class but targets three metabolic receptors instead of one
articles.nri_angle: South Asians carry the world's highest metabolic disease burden relative to BMI — a drug matching bariatric surgery outcomes could transform obesity treatment for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
